signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK/BQK)
signals.signal: CBK Monthly Statistics Bulletin No. 297 (reference period May-2026, PDF created 10/07/2026) Table 25.1 shows Kosovo's bank branch network still GROWING against the EU decline trend: total ODC (commercial-bank) network units 200 (2022) -> 215 (Dec-2023) -> 227 (Dec-2024) -> 235 (Dec-2025) -> 234 (May-2026); staff 4,143 (Dec-2024) -> 4,184 (Dec-2025) -> 4,151 (May-2026).
signals.source_name: CBK Monthly Statistics Bulletin No. 297, Table 25.1
signals.implies: A physically expanding branch estate in a cash-heavy euroised economy is the classic branch-transformation window: Glory/Sesami teller cash recyclers (TCR = a machine behind/at the counter that accepts notes and re-dispenses them, cutting manual cash handling), self-service kiosks and NCR intelligent-deposit ATMs in the new units, plus Printec managed field services.
signals.likelihood: High - network additions are continuing month by month
signals.followup: Map the 8 net new units added during 2025 to individual banks (ProCredit, TEB, Raiffeisen KS, NLB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike) and pitch TCR + kiosk fit-out.

signals.signal: Cash is NOT retreating in Kosovo. CBK MSB 297: ATM cash WITHDRAWAL count (thousands, non-cumulative) Dec-2024 1,957 -> Dec-2025 1,990; May-2025 1,888 -> May-2026 2,029. ATM withdrawal VALUE Dec-2024 EUR 390.7m -> Dec-2025 EUR 404.8m. ATM CASH-DEPOSIT count Dec-2024 304.9k -> Dec-2025 342.1k, value Dec-2024 EUR 266.4m -> Dec-2025 EUR 304.9m. Domestic POS card payments (count, thousands) Dec-2024 3,283.4 -> Dec-2025 4,503.1 -> May-2026 4,858.1.
signals.source_name: CBK Monthly Statistics Bulletin No. 297, Tables 24.1.1 and 24.1.2
signals.implies: Rising ATM deposit volumes alongside flat-to-rising withdrawals is the exact economics that justifies cash RECYCLERS (an ATM that re-dispenses notes customers deposited, so cash-in-transit runs and vault float both fall) and NCR APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation; POS transaction growth of roughly a third y/y drives terminal refresh and TMS.
signals.likelihood: High - the deposit-flow trend is the strongest recycler business case in the region
signals.followup: Build a recycler ROI model on the published EUR 304.9m/month ATM cash-deposit value and take it to the top-5 Kosovo banks.

signals.entity: CBK 'Use of Bank Cards in Kosovo'
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2024] No 2026 edition exists as of 27/08/2026: the live CBK URL still serves the September-2025 edition with data as of 31/12/2024 - 21,548 card-accepting terminals, of which 635 ATMs (634 withdrawal, 53 credit-transfer, 377 cash-deposit-capable = 59.4%) and 20,913 POS. The device-detail breakdown (deposit-capable / credit-transfer / contactless split) is published ONLY here.
signals.source_name: CBK, Use of Bank Cards in Kosovo, September 2025
signals.implies: The 59.4% deposit-capable share means ~258 Kosovo ATMs are still dispense-only - a concrete, countable upgrade/replacement pipeline for NCR intelligent-deposit and recycling units.
signals.likelihood: Medium - a 2026 edition is expected around Sep-2026 on the annual cadence
signals.followup: Re-check the same stable URL in Sep/Oct-2026 for the edition carrying 31/12/2025 device counts.

signals.signal: GAP CLOSED - the 2025 annual device counts DO exist, inside the CBK Annual Report 2025 (cover 'Prishtina, June 2026', PDF posted under /wp-content/uploads/2026/07/), not in the card report. Chart 64 ATM terminals: 516 (2021), 534 (2022), 583 (2023), 635 (2024), 686 (end-2025) = +8.0% y/y. Chart 65 POS terminals: 13,836 (2021), 14,769 (2022), 17,187 (2023), 20,859 (2024), 30,259 (end-2025) = +45.1% y/y, +9,400 terminals in ONE year. Debit cards ~1.9m (+33.7% y/y), credit cards ~218k (+12.1%). 2025 flows: ATM withdrawals 23,642,504 txns / EUR 4,927,015,021; POS payments 62,056,621 txns / EUR 1,745,226,003 (+33.4% count, +29.8% value); e-banking 13,490,958 txns / EUR 27,787,477,193. Client accounts 2,729,820 (+7.5%).
signals.source_name: CBK Annual Report 2025, section 4.4 and Charts 64-68
signals.implies: A 45% one-year jump in POS estate (+9,400 terminals) is the largest relative acceptance-estate expansion in the Printec footprint this run - direct pull for Verifone/Castles terminals, a terminal-management system (TMS = central software that configures, updates and monitors every terminal remotely) and softPOS. Meanwhile ATMs grew only 8% (+51 units) while ATM withdrawal VALUE still rose to EUR 4.93bn/yr: the estate is being asked to move more cash per machine, which is the recycler/intelligent-deposit and OptiCash argument.
signals.likelihood: High - both series are published and still accelerating
signals.followup: Ask each acquirer (Raiffeisen KS, ProCredit, NLB, TEB, BKT) who supplied the ~9,400 net-new 2025 terminals and when the fleet's first refresh/TMS renewal falls.

signals.signal: CONFIRMED at primary source: the Western Balkans TIPS Clone instant-payment platform went live 20/07/2026 with the central banks of Bosnia & Herzegovina and Montenegro, and Banca d'Italia states the next onboarding phase is November 2026, when 'the Central Banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join the platform'. CBK's own Annual Report 2025 lists the supporting overlay services now being scoped on top of KIPS: QR Code, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee; the CBK also signed an agreement with the European Payments Council in 2025 for use of the SCT, SDD and SCT Inst schemes.
signals.source_name: Banca d'Italia press release 'TIPS Clone platform for instant payments in the Western Balkans goes live'; CBK Annual Report 2025 s.4.5
signals.implies: A hard ~Nov-2026 date means every Kosovo bank must be ISO 20022 / 24x7 instant-payment ready inside ~3 months: Printec instant-payments and ISO 20022 channel integration, plus the Proxy-ID/QR/Request-to-Pay overlay build, plus INETCO real-time transaction monitoring and fraud screening (24/7 instant settlement removes the batch window in which fraud used to be caught).
signals.likelihood: High - date stated by the operating central bank (Banca d'Italia)
signals.followup: Get in front of the CBK Payment Systems Department (director Lumnie/Lumni Rrustolli) and the KBA Payments Committee before the Nov-2026 window; ask which banks are in wave 1.

signals.entity: World Bank Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project (P507881), Component 3 'Catalyzing Faster Payments'
signals.signal: Component 3 is worth USD 5.0m of the USD 52m IDA operation and has now cleared its legal hurdles: Financing Agreement signed 23/03/2026 and ratified 10/04/2026 (ISR Seq.3, archived 15/05/2026, still 0% disbursed / 'not yet effective'). Its indicators are explicitly infrastructure-buying: 'Number of financial institutions investing private money to upgrade their infrastructure to the new FPS' 0 (Dec-2024) -> target 11 by Jun-2030; 'Share of PSP connected to the FPS' 0% -> 95%; 'Time to credit payee's account for domestic credit transfer' 28,800 seconds -> 10 seconds; electronic credit transfers 11,432,406 -> 30,305,020. The Procurement Plan approved 27/05/2026 (GPN 21/05/2026) so far lists ONLY four national individual-consultant posts (procurement, FM, environmental, social specialists, USD 30k each, contracts planned 07/09/2026) - the Goods / IT / non-consulting tables are still EMPTY, i.e. the technology packages have not been advertised yet.
signals.source_name: World Bank ISR Seq.3 and Procurement Plan, project P507881
signals.implies: An 11-institution, donor-funded obligation to invest private money in FPS-ready infrastructure, with the World Bank's own goods/IT procurement tables still blank and international open competition mandatory above USD 1.5m: this is the cleanest tender-pipeline entry point in Kosovo for Printec channel integration, HSM/PCI-PIN key management and terminal/ATM software work. Watch STEP for the first Specific Procurement Notice.
signals.likelihood: High - project ratified; procurement plan runs to Jun-2030 and goods packages must follow
signals.followup: Register for World Bank STEP/UNDB notices under P507881 and contact the Ministry of Finance PIU; the four PIU consultant contracts are planned for 07/09/2026, after which goods packages typically appear.

signals.entity: CBK / Constitutional Court of Kosovo - SEPA accession
signals.signal: SEPA accession is still BLOCKED and the CBK has now said so in its own annual report: 'The restrictions arising from the non-promulgation of laws due to constitutional review prevented the final application to SEPA and, consequently, resulted in the loss of the opportunity to keep pace with neighbouring countries.' The three laws (08/L-304 Banks, 08/L-328 Payment Services, 08/L-333 AML/CFT) remain under Constitutional Court review after a PDK referral on procedural grounds; no ruling had been published as of 31/08/2026. A replacement Draft Law on Payment Services was circulated by the Office of the Prime Minister in April 2026.
signals.source_name: CBK Annual Report 2025 (Governor's foreword / executive summary); Office of the PM draft Law on Payment Services
signals.implies: Kosovo is the ONE Western-Balkan market where the SEPA compliance wave (ISO 20022 messaging, IBAN/reachability, PSD2-style strong customer authentication, EUDI-ready eKYC) is dammed up rather than spent - when the Court rules or the new draft law passes, a compressed multi-bank remediation programme lands at once. Position now, sell on the ruling.
signals.likelihood: Medium - ruling timing is judicial and unpredictable; a re-legislated route is already in draft
signals.followup: Monitor gjk-ks.org for the judgment on the Payment Services Law and Kuvendi's agenda for the April-2026 replacement draft.

signals.entity: CBK Regulation on access of non-bank payment service providers to payment systems
signals.signal: The regulation adopted by the CBK Board on 25/11/2025 is live and published (PDF under /wp-content/uploads/2025/12/). It lets non-bank PSPs open a settlement account in the RTGS module of KIPS and settle payment orders directly, and sets CBK powers to suspend access (with immediate account freeze) where a participant fails to fund settlement or breaches the rules. The CBK Annual Report 2025 confirms the reform was drafted with World Bank technical support and recommends further alignment with Regulation (EU) 2024/886, and that a companion act improving KYC processes was announced at the 17/06/2025 National Payments Council, which also created Kosovo's first Open Banking Working Group.
signals.source_name: CBK, Rregullore per qasjen e ofruesve te sherbimeve te pagesave jo-banka ne sistemet e pagesave; CBK Annual Report 2025 s.4.5
signals.implies: New direct KIPS participants (EMIs, payment institutions, fintechs) each need what a bank needs but own none of it: Thales HSM and PCI-PIN key management, remote key injection, ISO 20022 connectivity, AML/KYC screening (IMTF Siron) and transaction monitoring. A greenfield buyer class rather than a refresh.
signals.likelihood: Medium - regulation in force; first non-bank direct participants expected around the TIPS Clone go-live
signals.followup: Ask CBK Payment Systems for the list of applicants/participants under the new regulation and approach each with an HSM+AML starter stack.

signals.entity: Kosovo Banking Association / Visa - Tap to Phone (softPOS)
signals.signal: A national Tap-to-Phone (softPOS = an ordinary Android phone turned into a contactless card terminal, no hardware POS) merchant-adoption roadshow ran through 2026: Pristina 16/04/2026, Prizren 25/05/2026, Gjakova 29/06/2026, Peja 27/07/2026, co-organised by the Kosovo Banking Association with Visa (Slobodan Lukic, Acceptance Solutions Lead Western Balkans), Helvetas, Sweden/Sverige and IMAA, with CBK Payment Systems Department director Lumni Rrustolli presenting the regulator's next steps. Banks presenting live T2P propositions: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo (Valdrin Islami), NLB Banka (Hasan Sherifi) and ProCredit Bank Kosovo (Hana Shehu). Separately, Apple Pay went live in Kosovo on 30/07/2025 after Google Pay [STANDING - dated 2025].
signals.implies: Three of Kosovo's largest banks are actively selling softPOS to micro-merchants - and the +9,400 POS terminals added in 2025 shows the demand is real. Printec softPOS/tap-to-phone plus TMS and merchant onboarding (eKYC/e-signature via Namirial) fits the banks that have NOT yet launched (TEB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike, Banka per Biznes) and the acquirers needing certified attestation and key management behind a phone-based PIN.
signals.likelihood: High - roadshow is running monthly and three banks are already live
signals.followup: Approach the KBA Payments Committee and the four banks without a live T2P product with a white-label softPOS + TMS + merchant-eKYC bundle.

signals.entity: CBK National Payments Council / National Retail Payments Strategy 2021-2026
signals.signal: The National Retail Payments Strategy 2021-2026 EXPIRES this year and the CBK reports its targets were exceeded: financial inclusion 73% and non-cash payments per capita up to 49. The National Payments Council (17/06/2025) recommended, for 2025-2026, intensified coordination on TIPS Clone and SEPA and explicitly 'increasing investments in technical infrastructure and data quality', concluding that '2026-2027 will be key for finalizing strategic projects'. New acts on NBFI payment-system access and on improving KYC processes were announced, and the CBK also reviewed the Policy on Oversight of the National Payment System (aligning to BIS/IOSCO PFMI) and extended the Account Registry regulation to cover safe-deposit boxes, authorised persons and beneficial owners for AML/CFT reporting.
signals.implies: A successor retail-payments strategy has to be drafted in 2026 and the CBK has already said the money goes into technical infrastructure - the moment to get Printec's recycler/kiosk/instant-payments/eKYC roadmap into the sector's plan. The Account Registry extension to beneficial owners and safe-deposit boxes is a concrete AML data-quality workload: IMTF Siron / FICO AML and digital-onboarding eKYC.
signals.likelihood: Medium - a successor strategy is due but not yet published
signals.followup: Watch bqk-kos.org for the National Retail Payments Strategy 2027-2031 consultation and submit a vendor input on self-service and cash automation.

signals.signal: Kosovo's euroised cash cycle is heavy and getting heavier, not lighter. CBK Annual Report 2025: the banking sector deposited about 62.1 million euro banknotes at the CBK during 2025, of which 20.65m pieces (33.23%) were classified unfit and shipped to euro-area banks; cash EXPORTS rose to EUR 2,373m / 44.0m pieces in 2025 (2024: EUR 2,084m / 38.3m; 2023: EUR 2,215m / 38.1m; 2022: EUR 1,700m / 32.3m; 2021: EUR 950m / 18.1m) against cash imports of only EUR 31m / 4.1m pieces. The CBK supplied the banking sector with 4.48m brand-new euro banknotes (20.16% of all notes supplied).
signals.source_name: CBK Annual Report 2025, Charts 88-91 and cash-quality section
signals.implies: A third of all notes banks hand in are unfit, so every deposit point needs fitness sorting: Glory/Sesami TCRs and NCR intelligent-deposit ATMs with note-fitness and authentication sensors keep unfit and counterfeit notes out of recirculation at the branch instead of at the central bank, and APTRA OptiCash sizes the float behind a EUR 2.4bn/yr outbound cash flow.
signals.likelihood: High - a five-year monotonic rise in cash export volume
signals.followup: Quote note-fitness/authentication-capable recyclers against the 33% unfit rate; the CBK Unit Against Counterfeit Money initiative is a joint hook.

signals.entity: Assembly of Kosovo / President of Kosovo - Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks
signals.signal: MATERIAL CHANGE vs the 'all three laws blocked' baseline: the Law on Banks 08/L-304 WAS promulgated - Presidential Decree No. DL-16/2026 of 20/01/2026, published in Official Gazette No. 2 of 27/01/2026, in force 15 days after publication (i.e. ~11/02/2026). Article 147 gives licensed banks and foreign bank branches TWELVE MONTHS from entry into force to comply (so ~11/02/2027), and foreign branches three years for Article 29(5)-(7). The law transposes CRR 575/2013, CRD 2013/36/EU and the BRRD recovery-and-resolution framework. Only the Payment Services (08/L-328) and AML/CFT (08/L-333) laws therefore remain caught in constitutional review.
signals.source_name: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No.2/27 January 2026, Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks
signals.implies: A hard ~11/02/2027 bank-wide compliance date on an EU-aligned prudential and resolution law forces reporting, data-quality and risk-system remediation across every Kosovo bank: Printec core/digital-channel integration, AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO) and managed services. It also removes one of the three SEPA blockers, shortening the runway once the Court rules on the other two.
signals.likelihood: High - the deadline is statutory and already running
signals.followup: Check gzk.rks-gov.net and the Constitutional Court docket for whether 08/L-328 and 08/L-333 have since been promulgated too; time bank outreach against the ~11/02/2027 adaptation deadline.

signals.entity: CBK Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management
signals.signal: Kosovo's DORA-equivalent is now BINDING. The CBK Board's Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (51 pages, signed by Board chair Bashkim Nurboja) entered into force on 15/09/2025 and obliges ALL CBK-licensed financial institutions to be in full compliance FROM 01 JUNE 2026 - a deadline that has just passed. It mandates 4-hour initial incident notification to the CBK Systems Oversight Division with a 72-hour follow-up report and updates until closure; the reporting template names ATMs ('bankomatet') alongside CBS, SWIFT, RTGS and ACH as the critical systems whose compromise must be declared. It also requires strong encryption standards and key-management controls for sensitive data in transit, secure-API key/token protection, server-room requirements and secure-coding/cryptographic-practice standards.
signals.source_name: CBK, Rregullore per sistemet e informacionit dhe menaxhimin e rrezikut kibernetik
signals.implies: A live, already-effective mandate naming ATMs as regulated critical infrastructure and demanding auditable key management: direct pull for Thales HSMs and remote key injection (loading ATM/POS encryption keys securely over the network instead of two officers at the machine), anti-skimming and physical ATM security, ATM/device telemetry and monitoring for the 4-hour clock, and INETCO real-time transaction monitoring.
signals.likelihood: High - compliance date already in effect, supervisory examinations follow
signals.followup: Offer a gap assessment against this regulation to Kosovo banks and to the new non-bank PSPs entering KIPS; ask CBK Systems Oversight how it will examine ATM-estate compliance.
